282	
283	# M1 — a tradeable ending, and the one claim on the map a venue actually quotes.
284	# It carries all three belief slots' worth of interest: the model's .61 and the
285	# market's .48 sit side by side, and the 13 points between them is the edge
286	# somebody would be trading. They are never averaged into one number.
287	BRENT_CONTRACT = Proposition(
288	    id="M1",
289	    claim='A Polymarket contract "Brent below $70 on 2026-10-31" resolves YES.',
290	    kind="market",
291	    resolution=Resolution(
292	        criteria="The contract's published resolution is YES.",
293	        source="Polymarket's own resolution of the contract.",
294	        by=_resolve_by(30),
295	    ),
296	    prior=Belief(p=0.40, lo=0.28, hi=0.55, owner="model"),
297	    beliefs=Beliefs(
298	        # Nothing computed yet: the same numbers as the prior. Was .61 (.45 to .74),
299	        # the number research report 02 §3 gives for the base world — a figure
300	        # from a sketch rather than from this engine. The gap worth looking at is
301	        # between whatever the engine computes and the market's .48 below, and
302	        # that gap is only honest once the engine has written the first number.
303	        model=Belief(p=0.40, lo=0.28, hi=0.55, owner="model"),
304	        # **Illustrative, not a live quote.** A real market belief is read off a
305	        # venue: the mid-price between the best bid and the best offer becomes
306	        # the likelihood, and the quoted spread becomes the range. Nothing in
307	        # this file talks to Polymarket; a price is fetched at run time in a
308	        # later stack, and this stands in for one until then.
309	        market=Belief(p=0.48, lo=0.45, hi=0.52, owner="market"),
310	    ),
311	    # A contract payoff, because somebody already sells this exact question. It
312	    # names the venue, the contract and the side, and it names no price at all:
313	    # what the contract costs is a live quote, fetched at run time, and a number
314	    # typed here would be stale the moment it was written.
315	    payoff=ContractPayoff(
316	        venue="Polymarket",
317	        # Illustrative. Polymarket identifies a contract by a long hexadecimal
318	        # condition identifier; this readable stand-in is what a reader can
319	        # follow, and the grounding stack replaces it with a real one.
320	        contract_id="brent-below-70-2026-10-31",
321	        title="Brent below $70 on 2026-10-31",
322	        # You make money when the claim comes true, so the side is the yes side.
323	        side="yes",
324	    ),
325	)
326	
327	
328	# M2 — the second tradeable ending, and a different sort of trade: a pair, held
329	# on both sides at once, rather than an outright position.
330	ENERGY_SHARES_LAG = Proposition(
331	    id="M2",
332	    claim=(
333	        "The energy fund XLE underperforms the S&P 500 fund SPY by more than 3% "
334	        "over 20 trading days."
335	    ),
336	    kind="market",
337	    resolution=Resolution(
338	        criteria=(
339	            "XLE's total return minus SPY's total return, over the 20 trading days "
340	            "ending on the resolve-by date, is below -3.0%."
341	        ),
342	        source="Published closing prices and distributions for XLE and SPY.",
343	        by=_resolve_by(45),
344	    ),
345	    prior=Belief(p=0.35, lo=0.22, hi=0.50, owner="model"),
346	    # Nothing computed yet. Was .54 (.38 to .68), the number research report 02 §3
347	    # gives for the base world — a figure from a sketch, not from this engine.
348	    beliefs=Beliefs(model=Belief(p=0.35, lo=0.22, hi=0.50, owner="model")),
349	    # A price payoff, because no venue asks this question, but two funds anybody
350	    # can trade move when the answer changes. The other half of the pair the map
351	    # shows: a contract at one ending, an instrument at the other.
352	    payoff=PricePayoff(
353	        # The pair, held on both sides at once: XLE (Energy Select Sector SPDR)
354	        # against SPY (SPDR S&P 500 ETF), dollar for dollar.
355	        instrument="XLE vs SPY",
356	        # `direction` says which side of the named instrument makes money when
357	        # the claim comes true. Holding the pair long — long XLE, short SPY —
358	        # loses if energy shares lag, so the position that pays here is the
359	        # short side: short XLE, long SPY.
360	        direction="short",
361	        # Three per cent, read straight from the claim: the size of the
362	        # underperformance the claim asks for. `move` is a fraction of the
363	        # instrument's own price, which needs no assumption about an entry price
364	        # — and having a separate contract shape next door is what lets it mean
365	        # only that.
366	        move=0.03,
367	    ),
368	)
369	
370	
371	# N1 — the ending that is real and cannot be traded. A map is allowed to finish
372	# here as long as it says why, out loud, rather than quietly stopping or
373	# inventing an instrument that does not exist. Saying "there is nothing to trade
374	# and here is the reason" is an answer, not a failure.
375	TALKS_RESUME = Proposition(
376	    id="N1",
377	    claim="Omani-mediated United States-Iran talks resume publicly.",
378	    kind="not_tradeable",
379	    resolution=Resolution(
380	        criteria=(
381	            "Both governments confirm, on the record, that a mediated round has taken "
382	            "place in Oman."
383	        ),
384	        source="The Omani foreign ministry's statement, confirmed by both governments.",
385	        by=_resolve_by(60),
386	    ),
387	    prior=Belief(p=0.22, lo=0.12, hi=0.36, owner="model"),
388	    # Nothing computed yet. Was .29 (.15 to .45), a hand-written guess.
389	    beliefs=Beliefs(model=Belief(p=0.22, lo=0.12, hi=0.36, owner="model")),
390	    not_tradeable_reason=(
391	        "No venue quotes a contract on a diplomatic round, and the nearest traded "
392	        "proxies are sanctioned Iranian assets that cannot be bought at all, so there "
393	        "is nothing to price this with."
394	    ),
395	)
396	
397	
398	# --- The arrows ------------------------------------------------------------
399	#
400	# Every arrow says why it exists, how hard it pushes, how long the push takes to
401	# arrive, what the push does over time, and whether the push survives its cause
402	# going away. The sentence in `rationale` is the argument for the arrow;
403	# `provenance` is the only receipt, and it is ours to write rather than the
404	# model's to claim. An arrow does not get to say how sure it is of itself.
405	
406	
407	# H → B — the trigger, and the other half of the showcase the branch sets up.
408	# A one-time repricing: once the transit data confirms the lane is open the
409	# risk premium comes out of the price, and it comes out once. Retracting H
410	# later does not put it back — that is what `trigger` means.
411	#
412	# The source attached here is real and was opened by hand on 2026-09-17. It
413	# backs the arrow's premise rather than its number: a fifth of the world's
414	# traded oil goes through this strait, which is why the strait has a price in
415	# crude at all. The receipt still says `argued`, because no retrieval step ran
416	# for this fixture — a person put the address in. `retrieved` is left empty for
417	# the same reason; it is the day our own retrieval step fetched something.
418	HORMUZ_TO_BRENT = Link(
419	    id="H->B",
420	    source="H",
421	    target="B",
422	    mode="trigger",
423	    strength=1.6,
424	    lag=2.0,
425	    shape="impulse",
426	    half_life=30.0,
427	    rationale=(
428	        "The war-risk premium priced into crude unwinds once transit data confirms the "
429	        "lane is open. It is a one-time repricing, not a standing discount."
430	    ),
431	    sources=(
432	        Source(
433	            url="https://www.eia.gov/todayinenergy/detail.php?id=4430",
434	            title="The Strait of Hormuz is the world's most important oil transit chokepoint",
435	            retrieved=None,
436	        ),
437	    ),
438	    provenance="argued",
439	)
440	
441	
442	# H → C — the sustain. Underwriters hold the rate down only while the lane
443	# actually stays open; the openness is the desk and the low rate is the apple on
444	# it. Lag 0: a rate sheet moves the same day, not two days later.
445	HORMUZ_TO_PREMIUM = Link(
446	    id="H->C",
447	    source="H",
448	    target="C",
449	    mode="sustain",
450	    strength=1.1,
451	    lag=0.0,
452	    shape="step",
453	    rationale=(
454	        "Underwriters reprice Gulf hulls only while the lane actually stays open. The "
455	        "low rate is held up by the openness, not caused once by it."
456	    ),
457	    provenance="argued",
458	)
459	
460	
461	# H → N1 — the weakest arrow on the map, and marked as such. The sentence below
462	# is a story rather than a mechanism: it cannot say which way the causality
463	# runs, because quiet diplomacy is at least as likely to have reopened the lane
464	# as the other way round. So the receipt is `asserted`, the weakest of the seven,
465	# and that is how the canvas will draw it. An arrow like this is kept rather than
466	# deleted because the ending it reaches is worth saying out loud.
467	HORMUZ_TO_TALKS = Link(
468	    id="H->N1",
469	    source="H",
470	    target="N1",
471	    mode="trigger",
472	    strength=0.7,
473	    lag=10.0,
474	    shape="ramp",
475	    rationale=(
476	        "A lane that stays open is the confidence-building step mediators point to, so "
477	        "a public round becomes easier to announce. Which way this runs is arguable: "
478	        "quiet talks may be what reopened the lane in the first place."
479	    ),
480	    provenance="asserted",
481	)
482	
483	
484	# C → B — the insurance step reaching the oil price, about a week later. The
485	# mechanism is the sort of thing that is written down somewhere, and the arrow
486	# still says `argued`, because provenance is the only receipt and it records what
487	# our pipeline actually did: nothing was fetched for this file. An arrow does not
488	# get to grade its own mechanism, and marking this one `documented` with nothing
489	# behind it would be rejected outright by the map's rules.
490	PREMIUM_TO_BRENT = Link(
491	    id="C->B",
492	    source="C",
493	    target="B",
494	    mode="sustain",
495	    strength=0.7,
496	    lag=7.0,
497	    shape="step",
498	    rationale=(
499	        "Lower war-risk premiums cut the delivered cost of a Gulf cargo, and the saving "
500	        "shows up in the physical differential within about a week."
501	    ),
502	    provenance="argued",
503	)
504	
505	
506	# B → M1 — the most direct arrow on the map. A contract on "Brent below $70"
507	# reprices within a day of settlements printing below $68.
508	#
509	# The half-life is not in the plan's table. An `impulse` with no half-life has
510	# no decay to evaluate, and the engine has to evaluate this arrow, so a number is
511	# supplied here, illustrative like the rest.
512	#
513	# **Tuned.** Was 14 days, chosen because the contract settles a month out. Now 30.
514	# The contract is written on very nearly the event B measures, so the repricing
515	# lasts about as long as the move does rather than unwinding inside a fortnight —
516	# and at fourteen days the push had faded to a quarter of full size by the day
517	# the contract is judged, so M1's tile read its own prior and the clearest chain
518	# on the map showed nothing.
519	BRENT_TO_CONTRACT = Link(
520	    id="B->M1",
521	    source="B",
522	    target="M1",
523	    mode="trigger",
524	    strength=0.9,
525	    lag=1.0,
526	    shape="impulse",
527	    half_life=30.0,
528	    rationale=(
529	        "The contract is written on almost the same thing the claim measures, so a run "
530	        "of settlements below $68 reprices it within a day."
531	    ),
532	    provenance="argued",
533	)
534	
535	
536	# B → M2 — equities follow crude, but slowly, which is what `ramp` is for: the
537	# push climbs across the three days rather than arriving all at once.
538	BRENT_TO_ENERGY_SHARES = Link(
539	    id="B->M2",
540	    source="B",
541	    target="M2",
542	    mode="trigger",
543	    strength=0.8,
544	    lag=3.0,
545	    shape="ramp",
546	    rationale=(
547	        "Energy earnings track the crude price with a lag, and the shares grind toward "
548	        "the new level over days rather than repricing in one session."
549	    ),
550	    provenance="argued",
551	)
552	
553	
554	# B → R — the feedback arrow: a price outcome changing what producers do. It is
555	# the only kind of arrow allowed to sit on a loop, and what keeps that honest is
556	# that it takes time — a fortnight here. An instantaneous loop is not feedback,
557	# it is a contradiction, and the map's rules reject it. Nothing computes with
558	# `reflexive` until stack 06; until then it is data on the canvas that the loop
559	# check sets aside.
560	BRENT_TO_OPEC = Link(
561	    id="B->R",
562	    source="B",
563	    target="R",
564	    mode="trigger",
565	    strength=0.6,
566	    lag=14.0,
567	    shape="ramp",
568	    rationale=(
569	        "A sustained run of sub-$68 settlements pressures OPEC+ revenue targets and "
570	        "brings forward a restraint announcement."
571	    ),
572	    provenance="argued",
573	    reflexive=True,
574	)
575	
576	
577	# R → B — the arrow back, and the one negative strength in the base map. It is
578	# negative because B is the claim "Brent settles *below* $68", which announced
579	# restraint makes less likely. This is an ordinary world-to-world arrow, not
580	# feedback, so it is not marked reflexive: once the loop's feedback arrow is set
581	# aside, this one closes nothing.
582	OPEC_TO_BRENT = Link(
583	    id="R->B",
584	    source="R",
585	    target="B",
586	    mode="trigger",
587	    strength=-1.2,
588	    lag=5.0,
589	    shape="step",
590	    rationale=(
591	        "Announced restraint tightens expected supply and props the price back above the threshold."
592	    ),
593	    provenance="argued",
594	)
595	
596	
597	def _checked(graph: Graph) -> Graph:
598	    """Give back the map, or refuse to load this file at all if any rule is broken.
599	
600	    A stored example that quietly stops being valid is worse than one that never
601	    loaded: everything downstream — the golden test, the canvas, the generated
602	    browser types — would go on using it and nothing would say why the answers
603	    had changed. So the check runs when this file is first read, and a failure
604	    names every fault at once, in the same words a user would be shown.
605	
606	    Args:
607	        graph: The map to check before anything else is allowed to see it.
608	
609	    Returns:
610	        That same map, once every rule has been checked.
611	
612	    Raises:
613	        ValueError: If the map breaks any of the rules, listing all of them.
614	    """
615	    violations = validate(graph)
616	    if violations:
617	        listed = "\n".join(f"  - {one.code}: {one.message}" for one in violations)
618	        raise ValueError(f"The Hormuz example is not a valid map:\n{listed}")
619	    return graph
620	
621	
622	HORMUZ: Graph = _checked(
623	    Graph(
624	        id="hormuz",
625	        propositions=(
626	            HORMUZ_OPEN,
627	            WAR_RISK_PREMIUM_FALLS,
628	            BRENT_BELOW_68,
629	            OPEC_RESTRAINT,
630	            BRENT_CONTRACT,
631	            ENERGY_SHARES_LAG,
632	            TALKS_RESUME,
633	        ),
634	        links=(
635	            HORMUZ_TO_BRENT,
636	            HORMUZ_TO_PREMIUM,
637	            HORMUZ_TO_TALKS,
638	            PREMIUM_TO_BRENT,
639	            BRENT_TO_CONTRACT,
640	            BRENT_TO_ENERGY_SHARES,
641	            BRENT_TO_OPEC,
642	            OPEC_TO_BRENT,
643	        ),
644	        hypothesis_id="H",
645	    )
646	)
647	"""The base map: seven claims, eight arrows, checked the moment this file loads."""
648	
649	
650	# --- The branch: "…but Iran is struck the next day" ------------------------
651	
652	
653	# S — the strike. It exists only on the branch; the base map has never heard of
654	# it. A tail in the plainest sense: unlikely, and it changes everything if it
655	# happens. The resolve-by date is the day after this example is set on, because
656	# the branch supposes the strike lands on 2026-10-02.
657	STRIKE_ON_IRAN = Proposition(
658	    id="S",
659	    claim="A confirmed military strike on Iranian territory.",
660	    kind="event",
661	    resolution=Resolution(
662	        criteria=("A strike on Iranian territory reported by at least two of AP, Reuters and AFP."),
663	        source="The AP, Reuters and AFP newswires.",
664	        by=_resolve_by(1),
665	    ),
666	    # Illustrative, from research report 02 §3. S has no causes on this map, so
667	    # its computed number would be its prior anyway.
668	    prior=Belief(p=0.06, lo=0.02, hi=0.14, owner="model"),
669	    beliefs=Beliefs(model=Belief(p=0.06, lo=0.02, hi=0.14, owner="model")),
670	)
671	
672	
673	# S → B — a trigger against the oil price, sharper than the arrow it is fighting
674	# and quicker to fade: a strike puts the risk premium back in the price within
675	# hours, which is why the lag is zero and the half-life is ten days rather than
676	# thirty.
677	STRIKE_TO_BRENT = Link(
678	    id="S->B",
679	    source="S",
680	    target="B",
681	    mode="trigger",
682	    strength=-2.4,
683	    lag=0.0,
684	    shape="impulse",
685	    half_life=10.0,
686	    rationale=(
687	        "A strike restores the war-risk premium in the oil price faster than transit "
688	        "data removes it."
689	    ),
690	    provenance="argued",
691	)
692	
693	
694	# S → C — a sustain against the insurance premium. Underwriters price the threat
695	# they can see today, so the rate stays up for as long as the strike stands,
696	# whatever the transit counts say.
697	STRIKE_TO_PREMIUM = Link(
698	    id="S->C",
699	    source="S",
700	    target="C",
701	    mode="sustain",
702	    strength=-2.0,
703	    lag=1.0,
704	    shape="step",
705	    rationale="Underwriters reprice on the threat, not on transit counts.",
706	    provenance="argued",
707	)
708	
709	
710	# S → H — **the showcase.** Read this one slowly, because it is the whole idea
711	# of the product in a single arrow.
712	#
713	# It is a `sustain` arrow, and it points at the claim the user asserted. A
714	# reopening is held up by the *absence* of hostilities the way an apple is held
715	# up by a desk, not caused once by the opening event. So the strait's openness
716	# **retracts** — even though the user supposed it true the day before.
717	#
718	# **Two different days, and the difference is the point.** The user's word is
719	# withdrawn on **2026-10-02**, the day the strike itself becomes true: that is
720	# the day the world changed, and it is the date the tile's badge names. The push
721	# does not arrive until **2026-10-05**, because this arrow carries a three-day
722	# lag. In between, H is neither supposed nor pushed: it reads its own prior of
723	# .35 again, labelled *withdrawn — no live push yet*. From the 5th the -1.9 lands
724	# and H reads about .07. The three-day gap is not a bug to hide; it is the honest
725	# shape of the answer, which is why every day of a claim's series carries a name.
726	#
727	# That is allowed because supposing a claim is a **timed assertion, not a seal**.
728	# "Suppose the strait is open, from 2026-10-01" cuts the arrows into H that exist
729	# at the moment the edit is applied, and it cuts nothing else, ever. This arrow
730	# did not exist then — it arrives with the edit after it — so it is live and it
731	# can push H back the other way. That is the whole reason the branch lists the
732	# supposition first and the insert second; reverse them and the arrow would be
733	# cut and nothing interesting would happen.
734	#
735	# Now look at H → B in the base map above. That one is a `trigger`: it fired on
736	# 2026-10-01, the risk premium came out of the price, and that domino stays
737	# fallen. Retracting H on 2026-10-02 does not stand it back up — the push simply
738	# keeps fading on its own half-life while S → B shoves the price the other way.
739	#
740	# One branch, both kinds of causality: the sustaining kind, where the effect
741	# needs its cause to keep holding, and the sequential kind, where the effect
742	# outlives its cause. Getting this pair right is the difference between a map
743	# that behaves correctly and one that merely behaves plausibly.
744	STRIKE_TO_HORMUZ = Link(
745	    id="S->H",
746	    source="S",
747	    target="H",
748	    mode="sustain",
749	    strength=-1.9,
750	    lag=3.0,
751	    shape="step",
752	    rationale=(
753	        "A reopening is sustained by the absence of hostilities, not by the opening "
754	        "event, so a strike withdraws what was holding the lane open."
755	    ),
756	    provenance="argued",
757	)
758	
759	
760	HORMUZ_THEN_STRIKE = Branch(
761	    # The identifier the spec's own worked example already points at: a child
762	    # branch in `spec/multiverse/branches-and-worlds.md` names this one as its
763	    # parent.
764	    id="br_hormuz_then_strike",
765	    label="Hormuz opens, then Iran is struck",
766	    # No parent: this branch forks straight off the untouched base map.
767	    parent=None,
768	    interventions=(
769	        # 1. Suppose the strait opens, from the day this example is set. The cut
770	        #    reaches only the arrows into H that exist right now; H is the
771	        #    hypothesis and has none, so it removes nothing. The supposition
772	        #    holds from this day rather than for ever, which is what lets step 2
773	        #    hang a live arrow onto H at all, and why this edit comes first.
774	        Do(target="H", value=True, at=FIXTURE_DATE),
775	        # 2. …but a strike happens. The claim and its three arrows arrive as one
776	        #    edit, so the map is never left holding a claim that causes nothing.
777	        #    Nothing about H, C or B is touched: this edit only adds.
778	        Insert(
779	            proposition=STRIKE_ON_IRAN,
780	            links=(STRIKE_TO_BRENT, STRIKE_TO_PREMIUM, STRIKE_TO_HORMUZ),
781	        ),
782	        # 3. Suppose the strike lands, one day after the strait opened. From
783	        #    here the two kinds of arrow part company — see the comment on
784	        #    S → H above.
785	        Do(target="S", value=True, at=_resolve_by(1)),
786	    ),
787	)
788	"""The branch where the strait opens and Iran is struck the next day: three edits, in order.
789	
790	A branch holds no claims and no numbers of its own — only the edits. Everything
791	it shows is computed from the base map plus this list, which is what makes the
792	original safe to leave untouched.
793	"""
794	
795	
796	TITLE = "Strait of Hormuz"
797	"""What this example is called on screen."""
798	
799	ONE_LINE = (
800	    "If the Strait of Hormuz reopens, what happens to crude — and what happens if "
801	    "Iran is struck the next day?"
802	)
803	"""The example in one sentence, for the list of stored examples."""
804

"""The Strait of Hormuz: one worked map, and the branch where Iran is struck the next day.

This is the product's one complete example, written as Python rather than as a
data file so that every number can carry a comment saying where it came from.
Stack 03a works the likelihoods through this map in its golden test, and stack
03b draws it, so it is built to exercise every shape the model layer defines:
all four kinds of claim, both modes of arrow, all three signal shapes, a
feedback arrow, all three belief slots, a base rate, evidence, both shapes of
payoff — a named contract and a move in a price — and a stated reason for the
one ending that cannot be traded.

**Every number here is illustrative.** Not one strength, likelihood, lag or
half-life was measured. They come from the sketch in
`docs/research/02-causal-modeling-formalisms.md` §3 and from the worked chapters
in `spec/graph/` and `spec/multiverse/`, and they are written down so the
machinery has something honest-shaped to run on — not because anyone has
established them.

**And this map is a curated example**, so its inputs may be tuned to make the
worked example rich and interesting rather than flat. Every tuned value carries
a comment saying what it was, what it is now and why, and the word **Tuned**, so
that searching this file for it finds every one of them. What is never tuned is
a **computed** number: `beliefs.model` equals `prior` on every claim here, which
is the truthful statement "nothing has been computed yet", and the engine's own
world is served beside this map. A number typed in by hand cannot say where it
came from, and that is the one state this product refuses to show.

That is also why no arrow claims a provenance of `documented`: no retrieval step
ran for this file. Arrows say `argued` (a mechanism was stated
and nothing was fetched to back it) or, in the one weak case, `asserted` (the
sentence is a story rather than a mechanism). Every belief is a range, never a
point, for the same reason.

**The sign convention, which is easy to get backwards.** A strength's sign says
which way the arrow pushes the claim *at its head* toward coming out true — not
which way the world moves. "Brent crude settles below $68" is made **more**
likely by the strait opening, so H → B is **+1.6**, even though the thing being
described is a falling oil price. The research report writes that arrow as -1.6
because it was thinking about the price; `spec/graph/link.md` settles it the
other way and the claim wins.

**Identifiers.** Claims use the short readable names the spec uses throughout:
H, C, B, R, M1, M2, N1, and S on the branch. An arrow's identifier is its two
ends joined by an arrow drawn in text — `H->B` is the arrow from H to B. That
convention is settled here, and it is the one
`spec/multiverse/branches-and-worlds.md` already writes in its worked example.

The claims::

    H   the strait is open to unrestricted transit for 14 straight days  (the hypothesis)
    C   the Lloyd's war-risk premium for Gulf transits falls below 0.4%
    B   Brent crude settles below $68 for five sessions
    R   OPEC+ announces output restraint                        (the tail: unlikely, heavy)
    M1  a Polymarket contract on Brent below $70 resolves YES              (tradeable)
    M2  the energy fund XLE underperforms the S&P 500 fund SPY             (tradeable)
    N1  Omani-mediated talks resume publicly       (real, and no venue prices it)

The arrows, with their sign, mode, signal shape and delay::

    H --( +1.6  trigger  impulse   2 days, half-life 30 )--> B
    H --( +1.1  sustain  step      same day             )--> C
    H --( +0.7  trigger  ramp     10 days               )--> N1
    C --( +0.7  sustain  step      7 days               )--> B
    B --( +0.9  trigger  impulse   1 day,  half-life 30 )--> M1
    B --( +0.8  trigger  ramp      3 days               )--> M2
    B --( +0.6  trigger  ramp     14 days, REFLEXIVE    )--> R
    R --( -1.2  trigger  step      5 days               )--> B   closes the loop

B and R form the one loop on the map. It is legal only because the arrow into R
is the market feeding back on the world — marked reflexive, and made honest by
taking a fortnight to arrive.

The branch adds S, a strike on Iranian territory, with three arrows::

    S --( -2.4  trigger  impulse   same day, half-life 10 )--> B
    S --( -2.0  sustain  step      1 day                  )--> C
    S --( -1.9  sustain  step      3 days                 )--> H   the showcase

The long comment on that last arrow is the one to read: it is where the two
kinds of causality part company.
"""

from datetime import date, timedelta

from katalyst.domain import (
    BaseRate,
    Belief,
    Beliefs,
    Branch,
    ContractPayoff,
    Do,
    Evidence,
    Graph,
    Insert,
    Link,
    PricePayoff,
    Proposition,
    Resolution,
    Source,
    validate,
)

FIXTURE_DATE = date(2026, 10, 1)
"""The day this example is set on. Every date below is written as a span from it.

Nothing in this file asks what today's date is. The example is meant to read the
same in a year's time as it does now, which it cannot do if its dates move.
"""


def _resolve_by(days: int) -> date:
    """Give the date that many days after the day this example is set on.

    Written as a span rather than as a date typed out in full so that a reader
    can see how long a claim has to run without counting on their fingers.

    Args:
        days: How many days after `FIXTURE_DATE` the claim is settled by.

    Returns:
        The date the claim is settled by.
    """
    return FIXTURE_DATE + timedelta(days=days)


# --- The claims ------------------------------------------------------------
#
# Each one is a claim that will be true or false by a date, judged by a named
# source. `prior` is what the model thinks about the claim on its own, before
# anything causes it. `beliefs.model` is what it thinks once its causes have
# pushed on it — and in this file it is **equal to the prior on every claim**,
# which is the truthful statement "nothing has been computed yet". The engine
# computes the real number and the world it produces is served beside this map.
# No computed number is ever typed in by hand here: a number that cannot say
# where it came from is exactly the state this product refuses to show.


# H — the hypothesis. The user typed "the Strait of Hormuz is going to open
# next week"; this is that topic turned into something anyone could score.
#
# H carries the **user's own belief** as well as the model's. That is where a
# hypothesis gets one from: the likelihood slider on the input screen, stored
# untouched in its own slot. The user here is more bullish than the model —
# .55 against .35 — and that gap is the argument the user is having with the
# tool, which is the reason the two numbers are never averaged.
HORMUZ_OPEN = Proposition(
    id="H",
    claim="The Strait of Hormuz reopens to unrestricted commercial transit.",
    kind="hypothesis",
    resolution=Resolution(
        criteria=(
            "At least 14 consecutive days of unrestricted commercial transit through "
            "the Strait of Hormuz."
        ),
        source="Lloyd's List transit counts.",
        by=_resolve_by(31),
    ),
    prior=Belief(p=0.35, lo=0.22, hi=0.50, owner="model"),
    # `beliefs.model` equals `prior`, here and on every claim below, and that is
    # the truthful statement "nothing has been computed yet". The engine writes
    # the computed number, and the world it produces is served beside this map;
    # a number typed in by hand could not say where it came from, which is the
    # one thing this product must never show.
    beliefs=Beliefs(
        model=Belief(p=0.35, lo=0.22, hi=0.50, owner="model"),
        user=Belief(p=0.55, lo=0.40, hi=0.70, owner="user"),
    ),
    # The outside view the prior starts from: of the Hormuz disruption episodes
    # since 1980, 7 of 9 ended within 90 days. The count comes from research
    # report 02 §3, which cites nothing for it, so `sources` is empty — and an
    # empty source list means exactly that nobody has checked the count, which
    # is why nothing downstream of it may call itself documented. The prior sits
    # well below 7-in-9 because this claim asks for 14 *consecutive* days inside
    # one month, which is a harder test than an episode merely ending.
    base_rate=BaseRate(
        reference_class=(
            "Closure or disruption episodes in the Strait of Hormuz since 1980 that "
            "ended within 90 days."
        ),
        k=7,
        n=9,
        sources=(),
    ),
    # Two published items, one each way. Both are illustrative items for a
    # worked example set in October 2026, so neither address is a specific
    # article — inventing an article address that resolves to nothing is the one
    # thing this product must never do. Each points instead at the publication
    # that would carry such a report, and both addresses were opened by hand on
    # 2026-09-17. Nothing here moves a number: evidence is the audit trail
    # beside the likelihood, not an input to it.
    evidence=(
        Evidence(
            claim="An Omani-mediated round is reported, with both sides attending.",
            url="https://www.bbc.com/news/world/middle_east",
            direction=1,
            weight=0.3,
        ),
        Evidence(
            claim="Three tankers remain held and no release has been announced.",
            url="https://www.lloydslist.com/",
            direction=-1,
            weight=0.4,
        ),
    ),
)

def _checked(graph: Graph) -> Graph:
    """Give back the map, or refuse to load this file at all if any rule is broken.

    A stored example that quietly stops being valid is worse than one that never
    loaded: everything downstream — the golden test, the canvas, the generated
    browser types — would go on using it and nothing would say why the answers
    had changed. So the check runs when this file is first read, and a failure
    names every fault at once, in the same words a user would be shown.

    Args:
        graph: The map to check before anything else is allowed to see it.

    Returns:
        That same map, once every rule has been checked.

    Raises:
        ValueError: If the map breaks any of the rules, listing all of them.
    """
    violations = validate(graph)
    if violations:
        listed = "\n".join(f"  - {one.code}: {one.message}" for one in violations)
        raise ValueError(f"The Hormuz example is not a valid map:\n{listed}")
    return graph


HORMUZ: Graph = _checked(
    Graph(
        id="hormuz",
        propositions=(
            HORMUZ_OPEN,
            WAR_RISK_PREMIUM_FALLS,
            BRENT_BELOW_68,
            OPEC_RESTRAINT,
            BRENT_CONTRACT,
            ENERGY_SHARES_LAG,
            TALKS_RESUME,
        ),
        links=(
            HORMUZ_TO_BRENT,
            HORMUZ_TO_PREMIUM,
            HORMUZ_TO_TALKS,
            PREMIUM_TO_BRENT,
            BRENT_TO_CONTRACT,
            BRENT_TO_ENERGY_SHARES,
            BRENT_TO_OPEC,
            OPEC_TO_BRENT,
        ),
        hypothesis_id="H",
    )
)
"""The base map: seven claims, eight arrows, checked the moment this file loads."""


# --- The branch: "…but Iran is struck the next day" ------------------------


# S — the strike. It exists only on the branch; the base map has never heard of
# it. A tail in the plainest sense: unlikely, and it changes everything if it
# happens. The resolve-by date is the day after this example is set on, because
# the branch supposes the strike lands on 2026-10-02.
STRIKE_ON_IRAN = Proposition(
    id="S",
    claim="A confirmed military strike on Iranian territory.",
    kind="event",
    resolution=Resolution(
        criteria=("A strike on Iranian territory reported by at least two of AP, Reuters and AFP."),
        source="The AP, Reuters and AFP newswires.",
        by=_resolve_by(1),
    ),
    # Illustrative, from research report 02 §3. S has no causes on this map, so
    # its computed number would be its prior anyway.
    prior=Belief(p=0.06, lo=0.02, hi=0.14, owner="model"),
    beliefs=Beliefs(model=Belief(p=0.06, lo=0.02, hi=0.14, owner="model")),
)


# S → B — a trigger against the oil price, sharper than the arrow it is fighting
# and quicker to fade: a strike puts the risk premium back in the price within
# hours, which is why the lag is zero and the half-life is ten days rather than
# thirty.
STRIKE_TO_BRENT = Link(
    id="S->B",
    source="S",
    target="B",
    mode="trigger",
    strength=-2.4,
    lag=0.0,
    shape="impulse",
    half_life=10.0,
    rationale=(
        "A strike restores the war-risk premium in the oil price faster than transit "
        "data removes it."
    ),
    provenance="argued",
)


# S → C — a sustain against the insurance premium. Underwriters price the threat
# they can see today, so the rate stays up for as long as the strike stands,
# whatever the transit counts say.
STRIKE_TO_PREMIUM = Link(
    id="S->C",
    source="S",
    target="C",
    mode="sustain",
    strength=-2.0,
    lag=1.0,
    shape="step",
    rationale="Underwriters reprice on the threat, not on transit counts.",
    provenance="argued",
)


# S → H — **the showcase.** Read this one slowly, because it is the whole idea
# of the product in a single arrow.
#
# It is a `sustain` arrow, and it points at the claim the user asserted. A
# reopening is held up by the *absence* of hostilities the way an apple is held
# up by a desk, not caused once by the opening event. So the strait's openness
# **retracts** — even though the user supposed it true the day before.
#
# **Two different days, and the difference is the point.** The user's word is
# withdrawn on **2026-10-02**, the day the strike itself becomes true: that is
# the day the world changed, and it is the date the tile's badge names. The push
# does not arrive until **2026-10-05**, because this arrow carries a three-day
# lag. In between, H is neither supposed nor pushed: it reads its own prior of
# .35 again, labelled *withdrawn — no live push yet*. From the 5th the -1.9 lands
# and H reads about .07. The three-day gap is not a bug to hide; it is the honest
# shape of the answer, which is why every day of a claim's series carries a name.
#
# That is allowed because supposing a claim is a **timed assertion, not a seal**.
# "Suppose the strait is open, from 2026-10-01" cuts the arrows into H that exist
# at the moment the edit is applied, and it cuts nothing else, ever. This arrow
# did not exist then — it arrives with the edit after it — so it is live and it
# can push H back the other way. That is the whole reason the branch lists the
# supposition first and the insert second; reverse them and the arrow would be
# cut and nothing interesting would happen.
#
# Now look at H → B in the base map above. That one is a `trigger`: it fired on
# 2026-10-01, the risk premium came out of the price, and that domino stays
# fallen. Retracting H on 2026-10-02 does not stand it back up — the push simply
# keeps fading on its own half-life while S → B shoves the price the other way.
#
# One branch, both kinds of causality: the sustaining kind, where the effect
# needs its cause to keep holding, and the sequential kind, where the effect
# outlives its cause. Getting this pair right is the difference between a map
# that behaves correctly and one that merely behaves plausibly.
STRIKE_TO_HORMUZ = Link(
    id="S->H",
    source="S",
    target="H",
    mode="sustain",
    strength=-1.9,
    lag=3.0,
    shape="step",
    rationale=(
        "A reopening is sustained by the absence of hostilities, not by the opening "
        "event, so a strike withdraws what was holding the lane open."
    ),
    provenance="argued",
)


HORMUZ_THEN_STRIKE = Branch(
    # The identifier the spec's own worked example already points at: a child
    # branch in `spec/multiverse/branches-and-worlds.md` names this one as its
    # parent.
    id="br_hormuz_then_strike",
    label="Hormuz opens, then Iran is struck",
    # No parent: this branch forks straight off the untouched base map.
    parent=None,
    interventions=(
        # 1. Suppose the strait opens, from the day this example is set. The cut
        #    reaches only the arrows into H that exist right now; H is the
        #    hypothesis and has none, so it removes nothing. The supposition
        #    holds from this day rather than for ever, which is what lets step 2
        #    hang a live arrow onto H at all, and why this edit comes first.
        Do(target="H", value=True, at=FIXTURE_DATE),
        # 2. …but a strike happens. The claim and its three arrows arrive as one
        #    edit, so the map is never left holding a claim that causes nothing.
        #    Nothing about H, C or B is touched: this edit only adds.
        Insert(
            proposition=STRIKE_ON_IRAN,
            links=(STRIKE_TO_BRENT, STRIKE_TO_PREMIUM, STRIKE_TO_HORMUZ),
        ),
        # 3. Suppose the strike lands, one day after the strait opened. From
        #    here the two kinds of arrow part company — see the comment on
        #    S → H above.
        Do(target="S", value=True, at=_resolve_by(1)),
    ),
)
"""The branch where the strait opens and Iran is struck the next day: three edits, in order.

A branch holds no claims and no numbers of its own — only the edits. Everything
it shows is computed from the base map plus this list, which is what makes the
original safe to leave untouched.
"""


TITLE = "Strait of Hormuz"
"""What this example is called on screen."""

ONE_LINE = (
    "If the Strait of Hormuz reopens, what happens to crude — and what happens if "
    "Iran is struck the next day?"
)
"""The example in one sentence, for the list of stored examples."""

"""Fetching facts from the outside world and attaching them to the map as citations.

What this layer is for
----------------------
Everything that reaches outside this process for a fact: a web search behind the
model's own answers, a market price, an economic series. Each thing it fetches
comes back with the address it came from and the moment it was read, so a number
on the screen can always say where it came from.

What this layer must never do
-----------------------------
- Never decide whether a map is valid, and never change one. It supplies facts;
  `katalyst.domain` decides what they mean.
- Never invent a source. A claim with no address attached is not documented, and
  saying otherwise is the one thing this layer cannot be allowed to do.
- Never read an environment variable directly; ask `katalyst.settings` instead.
- Never import from `katalyst.api`.

Nothing lives here yet. Stack 04 adds search behind generation; stack 05 adds
the market and economic-data adapters.
"""

60	from pydantic import BaseModel, ConfigDict, Field
61	
62	from katalyst.domain.belief import Belief
63	from katalyst.domain.graph import Graph
64	from katalyst.domain.ids import BranchId, LinkId, PropositionId
65	from katalyst.domain.link import Link
66	from katalyst.domain.patch import Assignment
67	from katalyst.domain.proposition import Proposition
68	from katalyst.domain.validity import _name_of
69	
70	Numbers = NDArray[numpy.float64]
71	"""An array of ordinary numbers. Written down once because it appears everywhere below."""
72	
73	Flags = NDArray[numpy.bool_]
74	"""An array of true-or-false values: which draws a claim came out true in."""
75	
76	Draws = NDArray[numpy.float32]
77	"""One number per draw, kept to about seven digits rather than about sixteen.
78	
79	Sixteen thousand draws times a claim times a day is a great many numbers, and
80	holding each to seven digits rather than sixteen runs about three times quicker
81	and takes half the memory. Nothing visible changes: every number this product
82	shows is rounded to two significant figures, and every average, spread and
83	percentile below is still worked out to the full sixteen.
84	"""
85	
86	DRAWING = numpy.float32
87	"""How much precision one draw is kept to. See `Draws`."""
88	
89	
90	SeriesState = Literal["sampled", "supposed", "withdrawn", "pushed"]
91	"""What a claim's day is, in one word.
92	
93	`sampled` — the ordinary case: no supposition has ever touched this claim.
94	`supposed` — a supposition is holding; the claim is true in every draw and the
95	tile shows a word rather than a number.
96	`withdrawn` — the supposition has been undermined and no opposing push has
97	arrived yet, so the claim reads its own prior again.
98	`pushed` — an opposing push is live.
99	"""
100	
101	PARAMS_STREAM = 1
102	"""Which stream of random numbers picks the versions of the map. Never sees the branch."""
103	
104	WORLDS_STREAM = 2
105	"""Which stream of random numbers rolls the dice inside one version."""
106	
107	NINETIETH_PERCENTILE = 1.2816
108	"""How many standard deviations out a bell curve's 10th and 90th percentiles sit."""
109	
110	SERIES_CAP = 180
111	"""The most points a claim's series ever carries, however long the window is."""
112	
113	LOWEST_SURVIVAL = 0.02
114	"""Below this share of worlds surviving an observation, the world warns loudly."""
115	
116	NOTHING_ADDED: Mapping[LinkId, int] = MappingProxyType({})
117	"""What "nobody said which edit added which arrow" looks like: an empty, unchangeable map."""
118	
119	LOUD_STRENGTH = 5.0
120	"""A push beyond this is roughly 1% to 99% on a coin flip, and is worth a second look."""
121	
122	RANGE_BINS = 20
123	"""How many groups the versions are sorted into when working out where a band's width comes from."""
124	
125	TINY = 1e-9
126	"""How close to 0 or 1 a likelihood may get before the log-odds scale is asked for a number.
127	
128	A stated 0 or 1 has no log-odds — the scale runs to infinity there — so it is read
129	as "as close to certain as this arithmetic can say". Far finer than the two
130	significant figures anything on screen ever shows.
131	"""
132	
133	
134	class Retraction(BaseModel):
135	    """The end of a supposition: which claim, which day, and what undermined it.
136	
137	    A claim the user supposed true, and which a later edit has pushed back down,
138	    is never drawn as plainly true. This is what the tile's *Retracted · date · by
139	    "…"* badge is written from.
140	
141	    It records the day the **cause** became true, never that day plus the arrow's
142	    delay. Tying the end of a supposition to the arrival of the push would tie
143	    "do I still take your word for this" to a delay parameter — change a lag from
144	    three days to thirty and the supposition would silently outlive the news.
145	    """
146	
147	    model_config = ConfigDict(frozen=True)
148	
149	    target: PropositionId = Field(description="The claim whose supposition ended.")
150	    at: date = Field(
151	        description=(
152	            "The day it ended: the day the opposing arrow's source was settled, never "
153	            "that day plus the arrow's delay."
154	        )
155	    )
156	    by_link: LinkId = Field(description="The arrow that undermined the supposition.")
157	    by_claim: PropositionId = Field(
158	        description="That arrow's source — the claim the tile names in its badge."
159	    )
160	    by: int = Field(
161	        ge=0,
162	        description=(
163	            "Which edit introduced the arrow, as its position in the branch, counting "
164	            "from 0. Always known, and that is a theorem rather than a convention: "
165	            "supposing a claim cuts every arrow pointing at it at that moment, so any "
166	            "arrow that later pushes against it was added afterwards, by an edit."
167	        ),
168	    )
169	
170	
171	class World(BaseModel):
172	    """One finished answer: a map, the values its edits fixed, and every number worked through.
173	
174	    A world is a **computed result, never a source of truth**. It can always be
175	    thrown away and rebuilt from three things — the base map, the branch and the
176	    seed — and if a stored world ever disagrees with what those three produce, the
177	    stored world is the one that is wrong.
178	
179	    Every likelihood in `beliefs` is owned by the model and is read on that claim's
180	    own resolve-by day, which is the day the claim is judged and the date its tile
181	    already shows. `series` carries one likelihood per day so the spike and the
182	    fade are visible rather than hidden, and `states` says, for each of those days,
183	    whether the number is the ordinary sampled one, a supposition holding, a
184	    supposition withdrawn with no push yet, or a push that has landed.
185	
186	    **A claim whose supposition is holding reads 1 — exactly 1, range and all, or
187	    0 when it was supposed false.** That number is there so that a chain of claims
188	    multiplied together has a factor for it, and for nothing else: **no surface may
189	    print it.** Every reader looks at `states` first and prints the word *Supposed*
190	    where the number would go, because "suppose this is true" answered with a
191	    likelihood is a tool arguing with the person using it.
192	    """
193	
194	    model_config = ConfigDict(frozen=True)
195	
196	    base_id: str = Field(description="The map this world was built from.")
197	    branch_id: BranchId | None = Field(
198	        default=None,
199	        description=(
200	            "The branch that was folded on. None means the base world, the empty branch. "
201	            "Working the numbers through takes a map and the values its edits fixed, and "
202	            "never the branch itself, so whatever asked for the world writes this in."
203	        ),
204	    )
205	    seed: int = Field(description="The one number every random draw in here came from.")
206	    versions: int = Field(
207	        description="The outer loop: how many versions of the map were tried — how sure we are "
208	        "of the numbers we put in."
209	    )
210	    worlds: int = Field(
211	        description="The inner loop: how many worlds were run under each version — how the "
212	        "dice fall."
213	    )
214	    day_zero: date = Field(description="The day the window starts on.")
215	    days: int = Field(
216	        description=(
217	            "How long the window is, in whole days. Not the number of points in a series: "
218	            "a window longer than 180 days is drawn at 180 evenly spaced points."
219	        )
220	    )
221	    graph: Graph = Field(description="The map the branch's edits left behind.")
222	    assignments: tuple[Assignment, ...] = Field(
223	        description="Every value an edit fixed, in the order the edits were made."
224	    )
225	    retractions: tuple[Retraction, ...] = Field(
226	        description="Every supposition that a later edit undermined, and what undermined it."
227	    )
228	    beliefs: Mapping[PropositionId, Belief] = Field(
229	        description=(
230	            "The model's likelihood for each claim, read on that claim's own resolve-by "
231	            "day, with the range that says how sure we are of it."
232	        )
233	    )
234	    series_days: tuple[int, ...] = Field(
235	        description=(
236	            "Which day of the window each point of every series stands for, counting from "
237	            "zero. Ordinarily every day. Past 180 days the series is drawn at fewer, "
238	            "unevenly spaced days — every claim's own resolve-by day is always among them, "
239	            "so a tile's headline number is always a point of the line drawn beneath it — "
240	            "and then this is the only thing that says where those points sit."
241	        )
242	    )
243	    series: Mapping[PropositionId, tuple[float, ...]] = Field(
244	        description=("One likelihood for each of the days above, for the scrubbable time axis.")
245	    )
246	    states: Mapping[PropositionId, tuple[SeriesState, ...]] = Field(
247	        description="One named state per day, the same length as the series."
248	    )
249	    conditionals: Mapping[LinkId, Belief] = Field(
250	        default_factory=dict,
251	        description=(
252	            "The likelihood of an arrow's target with that arrow's source **supposed** "
253	            "true — never how often the two show up together. Empty on a freshly built "
254	            "world: it costs a whole extra run per arrow, so it is fetched one arrow at "
255	            "a time when something asks."
256	        ),
257	    )
258	    range_shares: Mapping[PropositionId, Mapping[PropositionId, float]] = Field(
259	        default_factory=dict,
260	        description=(
261	            "How much of each claim's band comes from not being sure of each claim's "
262	            "prior: range_shares[target][source]. Nothing on screen reads it yet; it is "
263	            "carried because the sample it comes from is thrown away otherwise."

from pydantic import BaseModel, ConfigDict, Field

from katalyst.domain.belief import Belief
from katalyst.domain.graph import Graph
from katalyst.domain.ids import BranchId, LinkId, PropositionId
from katalyst.domain.link import Link
from katalyst.domain.patch import Assignment
from katalyst.domain.proposition import Proposition
from katalyst.domain.validity import _name_of

Numbers = NDArray[numpy.float64]
"""An array of ordinary numbers. Written down once because it appears everywhere below."""

Flags = NDArray[numpy.bool_]
"""An array of true-or-false values: which draws a claim came out true in."""

Draws = NDArray[numpy.float32]
"""One number per draw, kept to about seven digits rather than about sixteen.

Sixteen thousand draws times a claim times a day is a great many numbers, and
holding each to seven digits rather than sixteen runs about three times quicker
and takes half the memory. Nothing visible changes: every number this product
shows is rounded to two significant figures, and every average, spread and
percentile below is still worked out to the full sixteen.
"""

DRAWING = numpy.float32
"""How much precision one draw is kept to. See `Draws`."""


SeriesState = Literal["sampled", "supposed", "withdrawn", "pushed"]
"""What a claim's day is, in one word.

`sampled` — the ordinary case: no supposition has ever touched this claim.
`supposed` — a supposition is holding; the claim is true in every draw and the
tile shows a word rather than a number.
`withdrawn` — the supposition has been undermined and no opposing push has
arrived yet, so the claim reads its own prior again.
`pushed` — an opposing push is live.
"""

PARAMS_STREAM = 1
"""Which stream of random numbers picks the versions of the map. Never sees the branch."""

WORLDS_STREAM = 2
"""Which stream of random numbers rolls the dice inside one version."""

NINETIETH_PERCENTILE = 1.2816
"""How many standard deviations out a bell curve's 10th and 90th percentiles sit."""

SERIES_CAP = 180
"""The most points a claim's series ever carries, however long the window is."""

LOWEST_SURVIVAL = 0.02
"""Below this share of worlds surviving an observation, the world warns loudly."""

NOTHING_ADDED: Mapping[LinkId, int] = MappingProxyType({})
"""What "nobody said which edit added which arrow" looks like: an empty, unchangeable map."""

LOUD_STRENGTH = 5.0
"""A push beyond this is roughly 1% to 99% on a coin flip, and is worth a second look."""

RANGE_BINS = 20
"""How many groups the versions are sorted into when working out where a band's width comes from."""

TINY = 1e-9
"""How close to 0 or 1 a likelihood may get before the log-odds scale is asked for a number.

A stated 0 or 1 has no log-odds — the scale runs to infinity there — so it is read
as "as close to certain as this arithmetic can say". Far finer than the two
significant figures anything on screen ever shows.
"""


class Retraction(BaseModel):
    """The end of a supposition: which claim, which day, and what undermined it.

    A claim the user supposed true, and which a later edit has pushed back down,
    is never drawn as plainly true. This is what the tile's *Retracted · date · by
    "…"* badge is written from.

    It records the day the **cause** became true, never that day plus the arrow's
    delay. Tying the end of a supposition to the arrival of the push would tie
    "do I still take your word for this" to a delay parameter — change a lag from
    three days to thirty and the supposition would silently outlive the news.
    """

    model_config = ConfigDict(frozen=True)

    target: PropositionId = Field(description="The claim whose supposition ended.")
    at: date = Field(
        description=(
            "The day it ended: the day the opposing arrow's source was settled, never "
            "that day plus the arrow's delay."
        )
    )
    by_link: LinkId = Field(description="The arrow that undermined the supposition.")
    by_claim: PropositionId = Field(
        description="That arrow's source — the claim the tile names in its badge."
    )
    by: int = Field(
        ge=0,
        description=(
            "Which edit introduced the arrow, as its position in the branch, counting "
            "from 0. Always known, and that is a theorem rather than a convention: "
            "supposing a claim cuts every arrow pointing at it at that moment, so any "
            "arrow that later pushes against it was added afterwards, by an edit."
        ),
    )


class World(BaseModel):
    """One finished answer: a map, the values its edits fixed, and every number worked through.

    A world is a **computed result, never a source of truth**. It can always be
    thrown away and rebuilt from three things — the base map, the branch and the
    seed — and if a stored world ever disagrees with what those three produce, the
    stored world is the one that is wrong.

    Every likelihood in `beliefs` is owned by the model and is read on that claim's
    own resolve-by day, which is the day the claim is judged and the date its tile
    already shows. `series` carries one likelihood per day so the spike and the
    fade are visible rather than hidden, and `states` says, for each of those days,
    whether the number is the ordinary sampled one, a supposition holding, a
    supposition withdrawn with no push yet, or a push that has landed.

    **A claim whose supposition is holding reads 1 — exactly 1, range and all, or
    0 when it was supposed false.** That number is there so that a chain of claims
    multiplied together has a factor for it, and for nothing else: **no surface may
    print it.** Every reader looks at `states` first and prints the word *Supposed*
    where the number would go, because "suppose this is true" answered with a
    likelihood is a tool arguing with the person using it.
    """

    model_config = ConfigDict(frozen=True)

    base_id: str = Field(description="The map this world was built from.")
    branch_id: BranchId | None = Field(
        default=None,
        description=(
            "The branch that was folded on. None means the base world, the empty branch. "
            "Working the numbers through takes a map and the values its edits fixed, and "
            "never the branch itself, so whatever asked for the world writes this in."
        ),
    )
    seed: int = Field(description="The one number every random draw in here came from.")
    versions: int = Field(
        description="The outer loop: how many versions of the map were tried — how sure we are "
        "of the numbers we put in."
    )
    worlds: int = Field(
        description="The inner loop: how many worlds were run under each version — how the "
        "dice fall."
    )
    day_zero: date = Field(description="The day the window starts on.")
    days: int = Field(
        description=(
            "How long the window is, in whole days. Not the number of points in a series: "
            "a window longer than 180 days is drawn at 180 evenly spaced points."
        )
    )
    graph: Graph = Field(description="The map the branch's edits left behind.")
    assignments: tuple[Assignment, ...] = Field(
        description="Every value an edit fixed, in the order the edits were made."
    )
    retractions: tuple[Retraction, ...] = Field(
        description="Every supposition that a later edit undermined, and what undermined it."
    )
    beliefs: Mapping[PropositionId, Belief] = Field(
        description=(
            "The model's likelihood for each claim, read on that claim's own resolve-by "
            "day, with the range that says how sure we are of it."
        )
    )
    series_days: tuple[int, ...] = Field(
        description=(
            "Which day of the window each point of every series stands for, counting from "
            "zero. Ordinarily every day. Past 180 days the series is drawn at fewer, "
            "unevenly spaced days — every claim's own resolve-by day is always among them, "
            "so a tile's headline number is always a point of the line drawn beneath it — "
            "and then this is the only thing that says where those points sit."
        )
    )
    series: Mapping[PropositionId, tuple[float, ...]] = Field(
        description=("One likelihood for each of the days above, for the scrubbable time axis.")
    )
    states: Mapping[PropositionId, tuple[SeriesState, ...]] = Field(
        description="One named state per day, the same length as the series."
    )
    conditionals: Mapping[LinkId, Belief] = Field(
        default_factory=dict,
        description=(
            "The likelihood of an arrow's target with that arrow's source **supposed** "
            "true — never how often the two show up together. Empty on a freshly built "
            "world: it costs a whole extra run per arrow, so it is fetched one arrow at "
            "a time when something asks."
        ),
    )
    range_shares: Mapping[PropositionId, Mapping[PropositionId, float]] = Field(
        default_factory=dict,
        description=(
            "How much of each claim's band comes from not being sure of each claim's "
            "prior: range_shares[target][source]. Nothing on screen reads it yet; it is "
            "carried because the sample it comes from is thrown away otherwise."
        ),
    )
    warnings: tuple[str, ...] = Field(
        default=(),
        description="Plain sentences the reader should see under the map.",
    )


@dataclass(frozen=True)
class Versions:
    """The version-by-version numbers behind a world, which never go on the wire.

    Comparing two worlds means subtracting them **version by version** — version 7
    of one against version 7 of the other — because both were built from the same
    2 000 sets of numbers, so that subtraction cancels the elicitation noise and
    leaves the edit. That needs one number per version per day per claim, which is
    millions of numbers on a map of any size, and no browser should ever be sent
    them.

    So they are not a field on `World`. They are recomputed from the world's own
    three inputs by `versions_of`, which is exact: the same map, assignments and
    seed give the same numbers every time, so a recomputed version is the version
    the world was built from.

    This is a plain frozen record rather than one of the data shapes, because it
    holds arrays rather than values and never crosses to the browser.
    """

    days: tuple[int, ...]
    """Which day of the window each column is."""

    weights: Numbers
    """How much each version counts, one per version.

    Every version counts the same unless something was observed, in which case a
    version counts by the share of its worlds that survived the observation — and
    then only for the claims in `reweighted`.
    """

    reweighted: frozenset[PropositionId]
    """The claims the weights above apply to: the ones an observation is evidence about.

    Every other claim is read with every version counting the same, because an
    observation joined to it by no chain of arrows and sharing no cause with it
    changes nothing about it at all.
    """

    priors: Mapping[PropositionId, Numbers]
    """The likelihood each version drew for each claim's prior, one per version."""

    likelihood: Mapping[PropositionId, Numbers]
    """Each version's answer for each claim, one row per version and one column per day."""

    inner_spread: Mapping[PropositionId, Numbers]
    """How much the worlds inside each version disagreed, per version and per day.

    What the noise correction needs. With this and the likelihoods above, a reader
    can rebuild any day's band exactly as the world reports it — which is how a
    difference between two worlds gets each world's band on whichever day it wants
    to read the change on, without a world carrying millions of numbers itself.
    """


def propagate(
    graph: Graph,
    assignments: tuple[Assignment, ...],
    *,
    as_of: date,
    seed: int,
    versions: int = 2_000,
    worlds: int = 8,
    introduced_by: Mapping[LinkId, int] = NOTHING_ADDED,
) -> World:
    """Work every likelihood on a map through time, and say how sure we are of each.

    Pure: no clock, no network, no global random state. The same map, values and
    seed give a byte-identical world on any machine, which is what makes a
    three-day-old screenshot reproducible from three values.

    The map must already be one the validity rules accept. In particular it must
    have no loops once feedback arrows are set aside, because the claims have to
    be worked through causes-before-effects and a map that runs round in circles
    has no such order.

    Args:
        graph: The map a fold left behind. Never changed.
        assignments: Every value that fold fixed, in the order the edits were made.
            When a claim has more than one, the last is the one in force and the
            earlier ones stay for the record.
        as_of: Day zero — the day the window starts on. This layer reads no clock,
            so the day is always passed in.
        seed: The one number every random draw comes from.
        versions: The outer loop — how many versions of the map to try. Each one is
            a coherent set of numbers this model would have stood behind.
        worlds: The inner loop — how many worlds to run under each version. At
            least two, or there is no inner spread to subtract.
        introduced_by: Which edit added each arrow, by position in the branch, so a
            supposition something undermined can name the edit responsible. Leaving
            it out is only safe when no supposition can be undermined; when one is,
            and its arrow is not in here, that is a broken promise between our own
            two pieces of code and it is said out loud rather than guessed at.

    Returns:
        One world: a likelihood and a range for every claim on the day it is
        judged, a likelihood and a named state for every day of the window, every
        supposition that was undermined, and a sentence for anything the reader
        should be told.

    Raises:
        ValueError: If a supposition was undermined by an arrow that `introduced_by`
            does not account for. The one thing this file raises for, and why is in
            `_retractions`.
    """
    setup = _prepare(graph, assignments, as_of)
    sample = _draw(setup, seed=seed, versions=versions, worlds=worlds)
    return _world_from(
        graph,
        assignments,
        setup,
        sample,
        _retractions(setup, introduced_by),
        seed=seed,
        versions=versions,
        worlds=worlds,
    )

    rather than storing them. The cost is one more run of the engine; the saving
    is that a world stays small enough to send to a browser.
